34.0.0.en: 1 Come near, ye nations, to hear; and hearken, ye peoples: let the earth hear, and all that is therein; the world, and all things that come forth of it. 2 For the LORD hath indignation against all nations, and fury against all their army: he hath devoted them to destruction, he hath delivered them to the slaughter. 3 Their slain also shall be cast out, and the stench of their carcases shall come up, and the mountains shall flow with their blood. 4 And all the host of heaven shall perish, and the heavens shall be rolled together as a scroll: and all their host shall fall down, as the leaf falleth off from the vine, and as a falling fig from the fig tree.

34.0.1.en: The prophet presents a general call to all the nations, that the world may listen, see and be silent, because the Lord has spoken. He proclaims God's judgment upon the nations that hold fast to evil, that perhaps they may return and heed His judgments, after God has been long-suffering toward them for a time.

34.1.0.en: It is like a call directed against the whole world, in which the Lord Himself enters as a party to the battle, declaring His indignation and the heat of His wrath upon all their armies [2]; for on account of evil they were exposed to slaughter and to the casting out of corpses until they stink; the blood runs on the mountains like water.

34.1.1.en: The prophet returns to affirm that God does not mean the sons of men; rather, the battle is between God and His angels and the devil and his angels. Therefore he says: "And all the host of heaven shall perish" [the hosts of evil in the heavens (Eph 6:12; Rev 12:7-9; 20:1-8)].

34.2.0.en: What does he mean by his saying: "And all the host of heaven shall perish, and the heavens shall be rolled together as a scroll: and all their host shall fall down, as the leaf falleth off from the vine, and as a falling fig from the fig tree" [3].

34.2.1.en: a. Some millennialist interpreters try to see in this a reference to the passing away of the old heaven, so that in the millennial reign a new earth and a new heaven may come into being.

34.2.2.en: b. St. Augustine sees that the heavens which are rolled together here as a scroll (a book) are the Holy Scripture, for he says: [The books of the two Testaments are called "the heavens"... I perceive and understand the Holy Scriptures which Thy servants wrote by the work of the Holy Spirit]. It is as though one of God's disciplines for the wicked who persist in their evil is their loss of the possibility of enjoying the host of heaven, that is, the power of the Holy Scripture, so that it becomes for them a closed book whose secrets they do not grasp in their lives, or it is for them like the leaves of a vine that have fallen and scattered, and like a falling fig from a fig tree. But for the children of God, the Holy Spirit opens their minds and their hearts and all their energies, so that they may grasp the power of the Word working in their depths as in their conduct.

34.2.3.en: Origen says: [The Holy Scriptures were written by the Spirit of God; and they have meanings not as they appear at first sight but other meanings which many do not grasp. For these (words) that are written are forms of certain mysteries and images of divine things. Therefore there is one opinion in the whole Church, that the entire matter is truly spiritual, and that the spiritual meaning contained in the Law is not known by all, but is known only by those to whom the grace of the Holy Spirit has been given in the word of wisdom and knowledge].

34.2.4.en: c. We can say that the earth and the heaven are a type of the body of man and his soul. The wicked lose the holiness and soundness of their bodies as well as of their souls. Their bodies become like mighty mountains, but blood flows from them [3]; they have the appearance of bodily strength, and perhaps bodily beauty and outward splendor, but they are like bodies stained with blood that bear the smell of death and stench. And their souls become like heavens that have lost all their energies (their host), closed like a sealed book... They have the appearance of courage, and perhaps of nobility and strength of personality, but when you come into close contact with them you find them narrow souls, broken by despair and corrupted by inner gloom, with a sense of isolation and deprivation.

34.2.5.en: This is the picture of the wicked man: he has a strong appearance outwardly but carries every weakness in his depths. As the psalmist says: "Fret not thyself because of evildoers, neither be thou envious against the workers of iniquity. For they shall soon be cut down like the grass, and wither as the green herb" (Ps 37:1-2).

34.3.0.en: 5 For my sword is bathed in heaven: behold, it shall come down upon Edom, and upon the people I have devoted to judgment. 6 The sword of the LORD is filled with blood, it is made fat with fatness, and with the blood of lambs and goats, with the fat of the kidneys of rams: for the LORD hath a sacrifice in Bozrah, and a great slaughter in the land of Edom. 7 And the wild oxen shall fall with them, and the bullocks with the bulls; and their land shall be soaked with blood, and their dust made fat with fatness. 8 For it is the day of the LORD's vengeance, and the year of recompences for the controversy of Zion. 9 And the rivers thereof shall be turned into pitch, and the dust thereof into brimstone, and the land thereof shall become burning pitch. 10 It shall not be quenched night nor day; the smoke thereof shall go up for ever: from generation to generation it shall lie waste; none shall pass through it for ever and ever. 11 But the owl and the hedgehog shall possess it; the crane and the raven shall dwell in it: and he shall stretch out upon it the line of desolation, and the plummet of emptiness. 12 As for her nobles, there is none there to call to the kingdom, and all her princes shall be nothing. 13 And thorns shall come up in her palaces, nettles and brambles in the fortresses thereof: and it shall be an habitation of wolves, and a court for the daughters of the ostrich. 14 The wild beasts of the desert shall also meet with the jackals, and the wild goat shall cry to his fellow; there shall the night settle, and find for itself a place of rest. 15 There shall the arrow snake make her den, and lay, and hatch, and rear under her shadow: and there shall the falcons gather, one with another.

34.3.1.en: It was the custom to smear swords with fat before the battle, so that they would not need cleaning after the killing of each of the enemies, since the grease keeps the blood from sticking to them. But the symbolic sword of the Lord is smeared, as it were, with heavenly wrath: "For my sword is bathed in heaven" [5].

34.4.0.en: The coming of the sword of the Lord upon Edom is like the knife of a priest slaughtering a flock unable to resist; it worked in the capital "Bozrah" [6] as in the rest of Edom, to offer sacrifices not for reconciliation but burnt offerings of judgment [5], upon which the divine curse has fallen.

34.4.1.en: This sword passed through all: the wild oxen and the bullocks with the bulls... that is, the violent men of war (the wild oxen) as well as the common people; the great with the small, for it is a general judgment, because all shared together in iniquity.

34.5.0.en: "Their land shall be soaked with blood, and their dust made fat with fatness" [7]; if the name "Edom" means "dust" (Adam) and also "blood," so their shed blood is mingled with their dust. They lived as dust, lovers of earthly and temporal things, and they perished by their blood.

34.5.1.en: God does all this for the sake of His Zion, His beloved people, whom Edom hates.

34.6.0.en: Finally he affirms that the destruction of Edom is complete [9-15].

34.6.1.en: "And the rivers thereof shall be turned into pitch, and the dust thereof into brimstone, and the land thereof shall become burning pitch. It shall not be quenched night nor day; the smoke thereof shall go up for ever: from generation to generation it shall lie waste..." [9-10], meaning that it turns into a furnace of fire that needs no fuel from outside, for its rivers turn into tar and its dust into brimstone, so that its land becomes a blazing fire that is not quenched by day or by night; its smoke goes up as a defiling odor like dark smoke, and its ruin continues throughout the generations.

34.6.2.en: It turns from a dwelling for men into a dwelling for animals and birds of prey [10, 11, 13, 14].

34.7.0.en: Instead of building, the line of desolation and the plummet of emptiness are stretched out [11].

34.7.1.en: Its leaders are lost; there are in it neither nobles nor princes.

34.8.0.en: Instead of fruits, thorns grow up even in its palaces, and nettles and brambles in its fortresses [13], a sign of the abandonment of the palaces and the disuse of the fortresses for a long time.

34.9.0.en: "There shall the arrow snake make her den, and lay, and hatch, and rear under her shadow" [15]. The nakkazah (arrow snake) is a serpent, one of the most malicious kinds of snakes, small in size but poisonous, living in regions of Africa and Arabia. However, what is stated here suits a bird rather than a snake, so some scholars see that what is stated here is a poetic description referring to the dwelling of deadly evil spirits in souls that resist God.

34.9.1.en: "There shall the falcons gather, one with another" [15], birds of prey that inspire terror..

34.9.2.en: Edom, then, refers to the soul that denies the faith and resists the truth; it falls under the divine wrath and becomes a furnace for itself, with no one to quench its inner flame and no one to grant it rest or comfort. It turns into ruin and loses its balanced thinking. It becomes a haunt for defiled thoughts and perverted emotions; sins make sport of it and demons play with it. Its life becomes dry as thorns and barren without fruit; it loses its beauty and its fortification, and turns into the darkness of a perpetual night without day or light [13].

34.10.0.en: 16 Seek ye out of the book of the LORD, and read: no one of these shall fail, none shall miss its mate: for his mouth hath commanded, and his spirit hath gathered them. 17 And he hath cast the lot for them, and his hand hath divided it unto them by line: they shall possess it for ever, from generation to generation shall they dwell therein.

34.10.1.en: "Seek ye out of the book of the LORD, and read: no one of these shall fail" [16].

34.10.2.en: He does not mean here the book of life or the book of judgment (Ezek 32:32; Ps 56:8; 69:28; Dan 7:10; Mal 3:16; Rev 3:5; 20:12; 21:27), but the prophecies which he proclaimed concerning Edom about its destruction.

34.10.3.en: Some observe that the prophet rarely issues a command, but here he commands, "Seek... and read," because the matter in his days seemed impossible and unreasonable. This prophecy was fulfilled in part after the destruction of Jerusalem by Nebuchadnezzar... and it is still being fulfilled every day with respect to those who resist the truth, until it is fulfilled in perfection at the last coming of the Lord, when the devil and all his hosts will perish.

35.0.s.en: 1. Turning the wilderness into a paradise:

35.0.0.en: 1 The wilderness and the dry land shall be glad; and the desert shall rejoice, and blossom as the narcissus. 2 It shall blossom abundantly, and rejoice even with joy and singing: the glory of Lebanon shall be given unto it, the excellency of Carmel and Sharon. They shall see the glory of the LORD, the excellency of our God. 3 Strengthen ye the weak hands, and confirm the feeble knees. 4 Say to them that are of a fearful heart: "Be strong, fear not: behold your God. Vengeance cometh, the recompence of God. He will come and save you."

35.0.1.en: Some scholars see that what is stated here concerns the state of the children of Israel after their return from the Babylonian captivity, but many see in it a description of the state of the Church of the New Testament, which enjoys the Lord Christ as her Head, who pours out His glory and splendor upon her. This is the opinion of most scholars among the Orthodox, the Catholics and the Protestants, although the followers of the millennial reign reckon this chapter a prophecy about it that has not yet been fulfilled.

35.0.2.en: The true believer who experiences the new life in Christ Jesus can experience the glory of the Church declared in his inner life, which is:

35.0.3.en: a. The turning of the wilderness and the dry land into a fruitful garden; for by the Lord's entering the heart and the Holy Spirit's dwelling in it, the inner barrenness is removed and the Lord's fruitful garden is planted, which gladdens the heart of God [1-2].

35.0.4.en: * It is clear that he is not speaking here about places outside the soul and the senses, but is announcing joyful good news for the thirsty soul, unadorned, through the symbol of the wilderness. As David says: "My soul has become toward thee as a dry land" [(Ps 143:6) Septuagint]. My soul thirsts for the Almighty, for He is the living God (Ps 42:2).

35.0.5.en: St. Gregory of Nyssa b. Perhaps the most important trait of the Church of the New Testament is "the joy of the Lord," for she lives exultant and inwardly rejoicing because of God's work in her. This line is clear in the whole book of the prophet Isaiah: the Messianic age is an age of joy, whereas there is no peace and no joy for the wicked who reject God's saving work.

35.0.6.en: "The wilderness and the dry land shall be glad; and the desert shall rejoice, and blossom as the narcissus. It shall blossom abundantly, and rejoice even with joy and singing" [1-2]. Joy, gladness and singing!

35.0.7.en: * He who has looked within himself to our Lord, and whose soul has been mingled with His light, let his heart boil over with joy.

35.0.8.en: The Spiritual Elder * Just as trees cannot grow if they do not drink water, so the soul, if it does not receive heavenly joy, cannot grow and ascend to the heights. But the souls that have received the Spirit and heavenly joy are those that are able to rise to the heights... for the mysteries of the Kingdom of Heaven have been uncovered to them while they are still in the body, and they have found boldness before God in everything, and all their requests have been fulfilled.

35.0.9.en: * The soul is always nourished by this joy and made happy by it, and by it ascends to heaven, for like the body it has its spiritual food.

35.1.0.en: St. Anthony the Great b. The glory and splendor of the Lord shine forth in the heart as a pledge of the eternal heavenly glory. "The glory of Lebanon shall be given unto it... they shall see the glory of the LORD, the excellency of our God" [2].

35.1.1.en: St. Macarius the Great speaks of this hidden glory that fills the life of the believer, to be revealed on the great day of the Lord, saying:

35.1.2.en: [By the renewing of the mind (Rom 12:3), the peace of the thoughts (Phil 4:7) and the heavenly love of the Lord (Eph 3:19), the new creation of Christians (2 Cor 5:17) is distinguished from the rest of mankind... Each one, in proportion as he is counted worthy of fellowship with the Holy Spirit by faith and diligence, in that measure his body will be glorified on that day, for everything the soul has stored up within it in this present life will be revealed on that day, and made manifest in the body... everything that belongs to the soul now will appear in the body on that day].

35.1.3.en: The Apostle says: "But we all, with open face beholding as in a glass the glory of the Lord, are changed into the same image from glory to glory, even as by the Spirit of the Lord" (2 Cor 3:7-18).

35.2.0.en: c. A man becomes a support to his weak brethren: "Strengthen ye the weak hands, and confirm the feeble knees. Say to them that are of a fearful heart: Be strong, fear not: behold your God. Vengeance cometh, the recompence of God. He will come and save you" [3-4].

35.2.1.en: Though life with God represents a personal, hidden relationship between God and the believer, it is not in isolated individuality, but through the life of fellowship between God and His one Church; each member supports his brother in the Lord so that all may be strengthened together as one bride. Every support you give your brother is a support for you personally, because he represents your hands and your knees.

35.2.2.en: * There is nothing that makes men so quickly defeated in trials and so collapsed as isolation. Tell me; scatter a company in war, and the enemy is not troubled in capturing and enslaving them one by one.

35.3.s.en: 2. Meeting the needs of the believers:

35.3.0.en: 5 Then the eyes of the blind shall be opened, and the ears of the deaf shall be unstopped. 6 Then shall the lame man leap as an hart, and the tongue of the dumb sing: for in the wilderness shall waters break out, and streams in the desert. 7 And the mirage shall become a thicket, and the thirsty land springs of water: in the habitation of wolves, in their resting place, shall be a home for reeds and papyrus. 8 And a highway shall be there, and a way, and it shall be called "The Holy Way." The unclean shall not pass over it, but it shall be for them. Whoever walks in the way, even the foolish, shall not err. 9 No lion shall be there, nor any ravenous beast shall go up thereon, it shall not be found there; but the redeemed shall walk there.

35.3.1.en: a. When he says: "He will come and save you. Then..." [4-5]; that is, when the Lord Christ the Savior comes, extraordinary things are accomplished, marvelous miracles and signs: "Then the eyes of the blind shall be opened, and the ears of the deaf shall be unstopped. Then shall the lame man leap as an hart, and the tongue of the dumb sing: for in the wilderness shall waters break out, and streams in the desert" [5-6].

35.3.2.en: Those who proclaim the millennial reign try to attribute this to the millennial reign, although the Lord Christ Himself used this text when He answered the disciples of John the Baptist, affirming that He is the expected Messiah (Mt 11:4-6). St. Augustine comments on this, saying: [It is as though He said to them: You have seen me, so know me! You have seen my works, so know their Maker... and blessed is he who is not offended in me].

35.3.3.en: God, who made everything good, came Himself into the world to renew His creation, mending what had been corrupted, and to restore to man his peace, health and joy. He opens his inner sight to behold the divine mysteries, and the ears so that they may delight in the divine voice and respond to His commandments; He gives the lame the ability to walk in the heavenly way, and makes the dumb speak inward praises... All this is by the action of the Holy Spirit (the waters and the streams), whom the Lord Christ sent from the Father...

35.3.4.en: * The prophecy of Isaiah is fulfilled not only in bodily matters but in spiritual ones also... for those who were formerly lame now leap by the power of Jesus like the hart. They were compared to the hart not without purpose, for it is a clean animal, an enemy of snakes, which cannot harm it with their poison. And so also with regard to the dumb, for they speak...

35.4.0.en: Origen b. "And the mirage shall become a thicket, and the thirsty land springs of water: in the habitation of wolves, in their resting place, shall be a home for reeds and papyrus" [7]. By this he means that instead of dryness there will be an abundance of water; for the dry land (the mirage) becomes a pool of water and the thirsty land springs of gushing water; in the habitation of wolves, where there is wilderness, there is water, so grasses grow and papyrus appears, which is found only in places where there is plenty of water.

35.4.1.en: The prophets often speak to us of the Messianic age as an age of waters (Isa 41:17-20; 43:18-20; 44:3-4; Ezek 47:1-12). The psalmist says: "There is a river, the streams whereof shall make glad the city of God, the holy place of the tabernacles of the most High. God is in the midst of her; she shall not be moved" (Ps 46:4-5).

35.4.2.en: * What is this river of streams? It is the overflow of the Holy Spirit, of whom the Lord said: "If any man thirst, let him come unto me, and drink. He that believeth on me, as the scripture hath said, out of his belly shall flow rivers of living water" (Jn 7:37-38). These rivers overflowed from the bosom of Paul and Peter and John and the rest of the Apostles, and from the believing Evangelists. And since these rivers overflowed from one river, therefore "the streams whereof shall make glad the city of God"....

35.4.3.en: It is clear that the courses of the river are understood to mean the Holy Spirit, by whom every devout soul that believes in Christ is sanctified to become a citizen of the city of God.

35.5.0.en: St. Augustine c. "And a highway shall be there, and a way, and it shall be called The Holy Way. The unclean shall not pass over it, but it shall be for them. Whoever walks in the way, even the foolish, shall not err. No lion shall be there... but the redeemed shall walk there" [8-9]. What is this "way" but the Lord Christ Himself, who offered Himself to His believers as a safe way in which no unclean one passes, but all in it are saints; even the foolish receive understanding and wisdom so that they do not err, and the enemy of good (the ravenous lion) cannot come near those who walk in it.

35.5.1.en: St. Cyril of Jerusalem speaks to us of our faith in the Lord Christ as a shield against the enemy of good, the devil, saying:

35.5.2.en: [Is there anything more terrifying than Satan? And yet we find no armor against him except faith, for it is an invisible shield against an invisible enemy, who aims various arrows in the middle of the night at those who are not on guard.

35.5.3.en: But since he is an invisible enemy, we have faith as a strong weapon, as the Apostle says: "Above all, taking the shield of faith, wherewith ye shall be able to quench all the fiery darts of the wicked" (Eph 6:16).

35.5.4.en: So when Satan throws a burning spark of base lust, faith shows the image of judgment and so quenches the wicked mind].

35.6.s.en: 3. A kingdom of joy and gladness:

35.6.0.en: 10 And the redeemed of the LORD shall return, and come to Zion with songs and everlasting joy upon their heads: gladness and joy shall overtake them, and sorrow and sighing shall flee away.

35.6.1.en: All the peoples of the nations who come to Him are anointed with the oil of gladness, and become a holy nation crowned with crowns of joy springing from victory. Sorrow and sighing cannot find a place in their hearts, but only outside.

35.6.2.en: This is the anointing of the Church of the New Testament, being the icon of heaven exulting in the Lord. Therefore it is said: "And the redeemed of the LORD shall return, and come to Zion with songs and everlasting joy upon their heads: gladness and joy shall overtake them, and sorrow and sighing shall flee away" [10].

35.6.3.en: * There is truly rest where there is no pain or sorrow or sighing, where there are no confusions or troubles or struggles or fear of the soul's bewilderment and disturbance, but there is the fear of God, full of joy.

35.6.4.en: St. John Chrysostom * Let us grieve here, meditating on the matter, so that we may not grieve there in punishment, but enjoy the eternal blessings... Let us delight in the things that surpass the mind in Christ Jesus our Lord (so that we are not troubled by grief).
